Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Suppose P is a finite group with (UP (1))Q ̸= 0. There is a tower of occurring finite p-groups · · · ↠ L2 ↠ L1 ↠ L0 = P, Γ = lim ← − i Li, with the following properties. (i) Every finite section A of Γ has d(A) ≤ l. Every closed subgroup of Γ is topologically generated by at most l elements; in particular Γ is finitely generated and Γ ↠ P. 8 (ii) For each finite collection of finite groupoids Y , at every sufficiently advanced stage L = Li inflation is an equivalence Fun(BL, Y ) ∼ − − → XΓ(Y ). (3.5) At those stages the evaluation maps give an isomorphism of DL-algebras in CQ, DL ⊗ AY ∼ − − → ∏︂ [α]∈π0XΓ(Y ) DL. (3.6) These isomorphisms are natural for pullback along maps of the selected groupoids. In particular, a common stage can be chosen for a finite diagram of finite groupoids, including both its bases and its total groupoids.
